RESEARCH AREAS

Nanoporous Materials:
Design, Synthesis, and Applications

We combine AI-guided design and synthesis to develop nanoporous materials for separation, catalysis, and electrochemistry.

IMaterials Design & Synthesis
01

AI-Guided Materials DesignAI 기반 소재 설계

We use data and AI to guide the design of materials with desired properties.

  • Screening of catalyst surfaces with universal machine-learning interatomic potentials (UMA, MatterSim)
  • Reaction pathways and selectivity from the computational hydrogen electrode and NEB
  • Synthesis–structure–performance data and active learning for composition search
  • Literature data extraction with large language models
02

Synthesis of Nanoporous Materials나노다공성 소재 합성

We synthesize nanoporous materials by controlling their composition, pore structure, and surface chemistry.

  • Sol–gel, hydrothermal and solvothermal synthesis with supercritical or ambient-pressure drying
  • Metal oxide, metal and metal sulfide aerogels (SnO₂, RuO₂, NiFe-based)
  • Silica and organic–inorganic hybrid aerogels with improved mechanical strength
  • Control of pore structure and surface area; BET, SEM/TEM, XRD and XPS
IIFunctions & Applications
03

Selective Adsorption & Separation선택적 흡착과 분리

We use interactions at pore surfaces to selectively adsorb and separate target components.

  • Electrochemical CO₂ capture and release on MnO₂ electrodes and the role of electrolyte cations
  • Amine-functionalized silica aerogels for CO₂ capture and heavy-metal or organic pollutant removal
  • Selective adsorption set by pore size and surface chemistry
04

Catalytic Materials & Reactions촉매 소재와 반응

We engineer active sites and interfaces to tune catalytic reactivity.

  • HER and OER catalysts for water electrolysis: RuNi alloy aerogels, NiFeSn oxyhydroxides, Pt clusters on SnO₂ aerogels
  • Ammonia oxidation (AOR) catalysts for direct ammonia fuel cells and nitrogen removal
  • Plasma electrochemistry for methane partial oxidation and NOₓ reduction
05

Electrochemical Materials & Interfaces전기화학 소재와 계면

We study charge transfer and reactions at electrode–electrolyte interfaces.

  • Electrodes and catalyst supports for water electrolyzers
  • Hierarchically porous metal oxides and sulfides for supercapacitor electrodes
  • SnO₂–carbon composite aerogels for lithium-ion battery anodes
